title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
requirement: A landlord may not take a deposit above one and one-half months' rent, must hold it in trust, pay interest to the tenant, and return it with an itemized list of deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
key_value: one and one-half months' rent; annual increase max 10% of current deposit
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in New Jersey where a landlord collects a security deposit; seasonal use or rental of not more than 125 consecutive days is excluded from the deposit-account rules.

applicability.per_tenancy: Security deposits for seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days) are excluded from the deposit-account rules.

exemptions: Seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days, with a permanent residence elsewhere) is excluded from the deposit-account rules.
penalty: Tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month's rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

title: Safe Housing Act security deposit return after domestic violence termination
requirement: When a tenant terminates a lease under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must make the deposit plus earned interest available for return within 15 business days and notify the tenant in writing within three business days where to collect it.
coverage_conditions: Tenants who terminate a lease before its expiration under the Safe Housing Act (domestic violence); does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.

applicability.per_tenancy: Applies when a tenant terminates the lease under the Safe Housing Act (domestic violence); does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.

quoted_span: If a tenant terminates the lease agreement prior to the expiration of the lease pursuant to the Safe Housing Act , (N.J.S.A. 46:8-9.6), the tenant is entitled to the return of their security deposit. Within 15 business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant's security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant's agent.
